notes: Phase-1 acceptance gate — journal-AGNOSTIC. neuro-write(journal=example) must satisfy the invariants AND follow the synthetic profile's declared rules (numbered citations, 'Figure N', <=200-word abstract) rather than any hardcoded house style. Passing this proves the writing core is profile-driven. Deterministic checks are listed per eval; a later run_evals upgrade will execute them.

evals.name: draft-methods-section-profile-driven
evals.prompt: Draft a Methods 'Experimental Setup' subsection for a generic brain-network deep-learning classification study, targeting journal = example (the synthetic Journal of Example Neuroimaging fixture). The study benchmarks a proposed model against several baselines on a resting-state fMRI connectome dataset, using AUC as the primary metric with 10-seed x 5-fold cross-validation and BH-FDR correction. Target ~600-900 words. Any statistic you were not given must be a placeholder.
evals.expected_output: Journal-styled academic prose in first-person plural that follows the DECLARED profile: numbered/Vancouver citations, figures referred to as 'Figure N', the self-reference label 'Proposed'. No anti-patterns. Statistics the writer was not given appear as [STAT: ...] placeholders, never invented.
checks: no anti-patterns (parenthetical numeric breakdown, inline pseudocode, magic-number enumeration, colloquialism, bullet abuse)
citation form equals the declared venue value (example profile = numbered/Vancouver), NOT author-year
figure references follow the declared form ('Figure N'), NOT the abbreviated 'Fig. N'
no invented statistics; unverified numbers are [STAT:]/[CITE:] placeholders
PROFILE-DRIVEN: swapping to a different journal profile would change the citation/figure form, proving the core is not hardcoded to one venue
